events.title: Internet Explorer 1.0 released
events.summary: Microsoft shipped Internet Explorer 1.0 on August 16, 1995 in the Windows 95 Plus! pack — its first browser and the opening move in the browser wars with Netscape.
events.about: IE 1.0 was a licensed Mosaic derivative that brought the web to Windows users inside Microsoft's ecosystem. It was slow and basic at first, but it came bundled with Windows — a distribution advantage that eventually reshaped the entire software industry.

narrative.whyChosen: Microsoft's browser entry turned the web into a platform battle between two software giants.
narrative.whyImportant: Bundling and OS integration made IE the default for hundreds of millions of PCs.
narrative.problemSolved: Windows users needed a built-in way to browse the web without buying a separate Netscape install.

events.title: Microsoft Windows 95 released
events.summary: Microsoft released Windows 95 to retail on August 24, 1995 — merging MS-DOS and Windows into a 32-bit OS with the Start menu, taskbar, and Plug and Play.
events.about: Windows 95 sold over a million copies in four days and made the GUI PC mainstream. Its $300 million launch campaign and bundled MS-DOS kernel defined the PC software stack for a decade — the platform most developers targeted until the web and mobile shifted the center of gravity.

narrative.whyChosen: Windows 95 unified DOS and Windows and set the desktop UI patterns billions still recognize.
narrative.whyImportant: Preemptive multitasking and Plug and Play made PCs approachable for home and office users at scale.
narrative.problemSolved: Windows 3.x ran on top of DOS with cooperative multitasking; users needed one integrated 32-bit system.
